task.name: A dev invocation started right after a gate failure is killed before producing output, consuming a retry for work that never ran
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A dev invocation started immediately after a gate failure is killed before it
produces any output. Three occurrences, all on issue-2681, all the same shape:

| gate event | dev starts | dev dies | recorded |
|---|---|---|---|
| VALIDATE timeout 10:42:41 (2026-08-30) | 10:42:42 | 10:42:53 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |
| VALIDATE timeout 00:17:53 | 00:17:54 | 00:18:07 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |
| VALIDATE FAIL 14:41:19 (2026-08-31) | 14:41:20 | 14:41:31 | `exit=-9`, `$0.000`, `output=0 chars` |

Run `0b14b21993ac` records the third:

```
14:41:20 ▸ DEV opus iter=2
14:41:20   Starting anthropic-opus-cli (model=opus, timeout=3600s)...
14:41:31   ⚠ 3 process(es) started by this invocation outlived it in their own
           process group(s) (pids=[27400, 27402, 27403]); killing them directly
14:41:31   ... anthropic-opus-cli done (11s)
14:41:31   [DEV] FAIL | exit=-9 | cost=$0.000 | output=0 chars
```

The story then aborts as a shared-infrastructure failure with no judgment
obtained, which is the correct report — the classification fix from #2807 is
working. What is not addressed is that the invocation is killed at all: the
iteration produces nothing, costs nothing, and the retry budget is consumed.

In the same run, the preceding iteration had backgrounded a long command and
returned while it was still running:

```
14:38:31 ↳ Bash: (make dev-check > /tmp/dc3.log 2>&1; echo "EXIT=$?" >> /tmp/dc3.log)
14:38:34 ↳ Bash: until grep -q "EXIT=" /tmp/dc3.log; do sleep 30; done; echo DONE
14:38:42   [DEV] OK | exit=0 | cost=$1.859 | output=81 chars
```

By contrast, a story whose dev delegated gate execution to the coordinator rather
than backgrounding it (issue-631, 2026-08-30) ran its post-gate-failure iterations
to completion.

## Expected behavior

An agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup belonging to work that preceded
it. Whatever a prior iteration leaves running is the prior iteration's to reap, and
reaping it does not reach a process started afterwards.

Where an invocation is nevertheless killed by the system rather than by its own
failure, that is distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced
nothing, and it does not consume the story's retry budget — a retry that never
executed is not evidence about the story, and spending an allowance on it converts
an infrastructure fault into an exhausted story.


## Diagnosis

Two `forge diagnose` runs were attempted and neither reached a cause. Both spent
their full 600-second budget still investigating and were cut off, so the cause
below is recorded as not yet identified rather than guessed at.

- **Observed symptom:** a dev invocation started immediately after a gate failure
  is killed before producing any output, recording `exit=-9`, `$0.000` and
  `output=0 chars`, and the story's retry allowance is spent on an iteration that
  never ran.
- **Evidence:** three occurrences, all on issue-2681, all 11–13 seconds from start
  to death, each beginning within a second of a gate failure — VALIDATE timeout
  10:42:41 (2026-08-30) → dead 10:42:53; VALIDATE timeout 00:17:53 → dead
  00:18:07; VALIDATE FAIL 14:41:19 (2026-08-31) → dead 14:41:31. Run
  `0b14b21993ac` records the third alongside
  `⚠ 3 process(es) started by this invocation outlived it in their own process
  group(s) (pids=[27400, 27402, 27403]); killing them directly` at the moment of
  death. In that same run the preceding iteration had backgrounded `make dev-check`
  and returned in 20 seconds while it was still running, whereas issue-631's
  post-gate-failure iterations, whose dev delegated gate execution to the
  coordinator, ran to completion.
  A fourth occurrence appeared on a different agent path entirely: `forge diagnose`
  run `431dfd5c8643` against this issue ended with its full artifact reading
  `CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event`, and run `a7b1dffca825`
  logged `diagnose ended without a result event with no priceable stream usage`.
  So the failure is not confined to a dev invocation following a gate failure.
- **Ruled out:** operator interruption, and leftover processes from earlier runs as
  a standing precondition — the host had no matching process group and zero zombies
  when checked between occurrences.
- **Confirmed cause:** not yet identified. Two diagnose attempts exhausted a
  600-second budget each while still reading the referenced run artifacts; run
  `a7b1dffca825`'s output ends mid-investigation on
  `"Let me check the per-story audit and full log for more detail on the DEV phase
  teardown fields and the preceding iteration."`
- **Affected code path:** not yet established. The teardown message at the moment
  of death is emitted by the agent-invocation process-group supervision, which is
  where an investigation should start.
- **Fix-success criterion:** an agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup
  belonging to work that preceded it; where the system does terminate one, that is
  distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced nothing, and it
  does not consume the story's retry allowance.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The plan carries its AC-critical root-cause risk into implementation. Step 2 hardens _release_group, but its current contract in src/theforge/process_group.py explains that a live pgid cannot be reused while the original group has members. Persisted cleanup already applies _identity_verdict, and tests such as TestReapVerifiesGroupIdentity plus the per-spawn lease isolation test already protect later/foreign processes. Moreover, the observed warning text is emitted by kill_escapees during the dying invocation's own teardown, not by _release_group before its killpg. Step 1's proposed retained-sidecar/later-group scenario therefore appears to duplicate passing coverage and need not reproduce the SIGKILL of the later invocation.
  Suggestion: Make the first step an end-to-end failing two-invocation reproduction that observes the later invocation's root pid being signaled and identifies the signaling call path. Scope the cleanup change only after that test fails through a concrete path; if no path can be reproduced, treat this as diagnosis work rather than committing to _release_group.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 6 tests only cost_usd=0.0, while current no-output negative-exit paths in runner_claude.py and runner_gemini.py produce cost_usd=None. zero_charge_no_model_artifacts currently requires exactly 0.0, so the test would not catch those real runner results failing to set unused_dev_iteration.
  Suggestion: Enumerate the cost-unknown Claude/Gemini paths in Step 3 and add runner/seam cases for cost_usd=None; explicitly decide whether system_killed overrides the zero-charge predicate or whether those runners can validly normalize this event to measured zero.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk #1 (root cause unproven). The plan has no branch for the case where Step 1's regression *falsifies* the pgid-recycle hypothesis, and it never touches the fourth occurrence the spec reports on a different path entirely — forge diagnose run 431dfd5c8643 ending in CLAUDE_STREAM_NO_TEXT: reason=missing_result_event with no process-teardown message at all. If the kill is not stale-cleanup, Steps 3-6 still land (the record and the refund improve) but the first acceptance criterion goes unmet.
  Suggestion: Have the dev agent run Step 1 first as a real falsification: reproduce a pgid-recycle window (prior leader exits, successor setsid's into the freed pgid, prior release path fires) before writing Step 2. If it cannot be reproduced, widen the investigation to the runner-side stream/result path shared with the diagnose occurrence rather than hardening process_group.py speculatively, and say so in the handoff.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 directly contradicts a documented rationale it does not mention. The _release_group docstring (src/theforge/process_group.py:568-572) explicitly argues that killing on membership alone is safe despite pgid recycling — 'a pgid is only reusable once its group is empty, and a group with live members has not emptied ... the check _identity_verdict makes for a record read minutes later is not needed for one read microseconds after our own wait returned.' That reasoning is what the fix has to overturn (it assumes the group never empties between the leader's exit and the membership read).
  Suggestion: Rewrite that docstring paragraph as part of Step 2, stating the window that invalidates it, so the next reader does not restore the old behavior on the strength of the comment.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 5 names the wrong audit fixture. CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION is 43 (src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py:155) and tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v43.json already exists; the plan lists v42. Any shape change to the audit record trips test_audit_schema_guard.py, which demands a version bump plus a newly committed fixture and MIGRATION_HELPERS entry.
  Suggestion: If Step 5 changes the record shape, bump to 44 and commit tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v44.json with the migration helper the guard test names; if it only reuses the existing agent_invocation_failures/infrastructure_failure keys, touch no fixture at all.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk #2 (a genuine timeout or stuck-pattern kill must stay a consumed, auditable attempt) has a stated mitigation but no assertion. Step 6 only asserts the system_killed refund path; nothing added would fail if the new negative-exit-code branch swallowed a real timeout, whose paid-for partial work must still charge the budget.
  Suggestion: Add the negative case to Step 6: a dev result with failure_code=timeout and partial artifacts must leave RetryBudget consumption intact and record dev iteration telemetry.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 must add its new category-or-code to the allowed set. AgentInvocationFailure.__post_init__ (agent_failure.py:346-351) raises on any category outside ALLOWED_FAILURE_CATEGORIES, and zero_charge_no_model_artifacts short-circuits on _MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILURE_CODES (agent_failure.py:239-240).
  Suggestion: Reuse CATEGORY_PROCESS (already the classify_failure_category fallback) rather than minting a new category, and confirm system_killed is deliberately absent from _MODEL_EXECUTION_FAILURE_CODES so the refund path stays reachable.

plan_structured.approach: Fix this as one lifecycle bug: make process cleanup prove invocation identity before signaling, then carry no-output external kills through runner results, audit, and retry accounting using the existing AgentResult.failure_code, agent_invocation_failures, infrastructure_failure, and RetryBudget.release_unused surfaces. Pin the behavior with a process-group race regression plus a coordinator seam test.

steps.description: Add a regression for stale cleanup not killing a later invocation
steps.details: Add a test around run_in_process_group, release_group_record, and/or reap_orphan_agents that creates a prior invocation with a retained sidecar or live survivor, starts a second isolated process group, then runs the prior cleanup path and asserts only the prior invocation's proven descendants are signaled while the second invocation remains alive.

steps.description: Harden process-group release identity before killpg
steps.details: In the live release path, do not let _release_group kill a non-empty pgid solely because group_is_alive/group_members_checked says something currently holds that pgid. Before kill_agent_group is called for a previously registered invocation, read the same-owner sidecar written by register_agent_group and apply the existing _identity_verdict-style leader/member fingerprint check; if identity is stale or unverifiable, drop or retain conservatively without signaling the foreign group. Keep kill_escapees limited to DescendantTracker.survivors, recorded observed pids with matching fingerprints, and lease_holders for that invocation's ProcessLease.

steps.description: Normalize external no-output SIGKILLs as system-killed invocation failures
steps.details: When a CLI subprocess exits with a negative signal such as -9 without the runner's own timeout or stuck-pattern path firing, and there is no text, tool trace, raw result, session, structured data, handoff, or model usage, return an AgentResult with a stable failure_code such as system_killed. Teach classify_failure_category and zero_charge_no_model_artifacts to classify that as a no-judgment process/system failure rather than as an agent that ran and produced an empty answer.

steps.description: Ensure unused system-killed dev slots are not charged to retry budget
steps.details: Use the existing classify_agent_failure, zero_charge_no_model_artifacts, CoordinatorResult.unused_dev_iteration, and RetryBudget.release_unused path for system_killed no-output DEV results. Preserve an audit-visible AgentInvocationFailure and infrastructure_failure before rolling back the recorded dev attempt, and ensure engine.py releases the just-consumed budget slot whenever _run_dev_phase returns unused_dev_iteration=True.

steps.description: Expose the distinction in audit records
steps.details: Make sure the run audit records the system-killed no-judgment event through agent_invocation_failures and infrastructure_failure with phase, category, exit_code=-9, failure_code, profile, and detail. Keep cost.agents/process_teardown semantics intact so a real empty-output model run remains distinct from a rolled-back unused invocation.

steps.description: Add coordinator seam coverage for retry refund and audit visibility
steps.details: Add a seam test where run_agent returns a failed AgentResult with exit_code=-9, cost_usd=0.0, no artifacts, and failure_code=system_killed. Assert the coordinator aborts as infrastructure_failure, records an invocation failure, does not record a productive dev result or telemetry for the unused attempt, and leaves RetryBudget counters/consumption_log as if the reserved iteration never ran.

criteria_mapping.criterion: An agent invocation is not terminated by cleanup belonging to work that preceded it.
Where an invocation is nevertheless killed by the system rather than by its own failure, that is distinguishable in the record from an agent that ran and produced nothing.
A retry that never executed does not consume the story's retry allowance.

risks.description: The confirmed root cause is still ambiguous; the likely pgid-reuse/stale-cleanup path must be proven or falsified by the new process-group regression.
risks.mitigation: Start with the failing lifecycle test and only harden the cleanup path that can reproduce or closely model the observed post-gate timing.

risks.description: A real agent timeout or stuck-pattern kill also uses signals and must remain a consumed, auditable attempt.
risks.mitigation: Classify system_killed only when the runner did not set its own timeout/stuck failure_code and no model/output artifacts exist.

risks.description: Rolling back dev_results for unused invocations can hide the event if the audit ledger is not updated first.
risks.mitigation: Record AgentInvocationFailure and infrastructure_failure before rollback, and assert both audit visibility and budget refund in the seam test.
